stories.title: U.S. Indicts Nicolás Maduro and Wife on Torture Charges
stories.summary: U.S. authorities have charged former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, with conspiracy to commit torture. This new indictment adds to existing drug trafficking allegations against Maduro and relates to the alleged torture of U.S. citizens during his presidency. The charges are part of a broader effort to hold Maduro accountable for human rights abuses in Venezuela.

stories.title: Russian Strike on Kramatorsk Buses Results in Significant Civilian Casualties
stories.summary: A Russian attack on civilian buses in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk has resulted in at least 30 to 33 fatalities, with many others wounded. The strike is part of a broader pattern of increasing assaults on civilian targets in Ukraine, raising concerns about the safety of non-combatants. Authorities have suspended public transport in the area following the incident.

stories.title: Anne Carson Wins Nobel Prize in Literature for Genre-Blending Works
stories.summary: Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for her innovative and genre-blending works that merge classical themes with modern narratives. At 76 years old, Carson is celebrated for her unique ability to draw on ancient Greek and Roman literature while incorporating elements of poetry, essay, and fiction into her writing.

stories.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Airports Result in Three Deaths Amid Escalating Conflict
stories.summary: Houthi rebels have launched attacks on two international airports in Saudi Arabia, resulting in the deaths of three individuals and injuring 36 others. The assaults are part of a broader escalation in the ongoing conflict, with the Houthis claiming responsibility for targeting civilian infrastructure. Saudi authorities reported intercepting two ballistic missiles aimed at the capital, Riyadh, shortly after the attacks.

stories.title: Mass Protests Planned in Madrid Following Death of Evicted Pensioner Maricarmen
stories.summary: Thousands are expected to march in Madrid to honor María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis. Abascal was forcibly removed from her home of over 70 years last month, and her death has reignited calls for action against housing injustices in the country. Many believe the stress from her eviction contributed to her passing.

stories.title: South Korea Recalls Ambassador to Ukraine Amid POW Dispute
stories.summary: South Korea has announced the recall of its ambassador to Ukraine following a diplomatic dispute over the public disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war. The South Korean government expressed concerns that this revelation could endanger the prisoners' families in North Korea and has demanded an apology from Ukraine, which has not been forthcoming. The situation escalated after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive measures if Ukraine does not respond.

stories.title: UK to Maintain Diplomatic Presence in East Jerusalem Amidst Tensions with Israel
stories.summary: The UK government has announced that its consulate in East Jerusalem will be rebranded as a UK mission, with a significant reduction in staff. Only seven diplomats will remain in the building, including the consul general, who will be leaving. This decision comes as Israel has stated that the consulate has 'ceased to function' in response to UK sanctions on illegal settlements in the West Bank.

Global protests are also occurring in solidarity with Gaza as the situation remains dire.

stories.title: British Police Acknowledge Unlawful Search Warrants in Case Against Former Prince Andrew
stories.summary: British police have admitted that the search warrants issued to investigate properties linked to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor were unlawful and must be quashed. A London judge confirmed this ruling, although the investigation into the younger brother of King Charles II remains ongoing. Andrew was arrested on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office.
